construction.definition: For integer T>=1, Psi(v)=0 for v<=1/2 and exp(1-(2v-1)^(-2)) otherwise; Phi0(v)=sqrt(e) integral_{-infinity}^v exp(-t^2/2)dt. Define bar_f_T(w)=-Psi(1)Phi0(w1)+sum_{i=2}^T[Psi(-w_(i-1))Phi0(-wi)-Psi(w_(i-1))Phi0(wi)]. Draw uniform Stiefel U in R^(d x T), U^T U=I, once independently of algorithm coins. R=230sqrt(T); P_R(z)=z/sqrt(1+||z||^2/R^2); h_U(z)=bar_f_T(U^T P_R(z))+||z||^2/10. Let a1,a2>0 be uniform upper bounds on ||H_h|| and Lip(H_h), justified below. Given ell,rho,delta,Delta>0 choose s=max{2delta a1/ell,sqrt(2delta a2/rho)}, A=2delta s, T=floor(Delta/(24delta s)), eta=1/4, finite integer d>=ceil(52*230^2*T^2*log(2*T^2/eta)), F_U(z)=A h_U(z/s). For kappa=L/mu>=6 set ell=mu, b=sqrt((kappa-3)/2), delta=3epsilon/(2b), g0=grad F_U(0), c=-g0/(2mu), and f_U(x,y)=F_U(y)-mu||y-bx-c||^2.
construction.hidden_objects: One hidden uniform Stiefel frame U. c depends only on its charged origin response. No unknown minimizer or unqueried derivative information is public.
construction.parameters: L>=mu>0; rho,Delta,epsilon>0. Coupled branch kappa>=6; require T>=3 and N+2<=T. x,y in R^d; x0=y0=0. The bounded-kappa decoupled branch is specified in the complete local proof.

oracle_realizations.choices_and_history: U sampled once fixes F,c,f and every exact response. Arbitrary measurable adaptive queries and terminal output from instance-independent coins; unbounded query locations permitted.
oracle_realizations.cost: One charged complete bundle; measurable transcript computation free. N lifted calls use N+1 baseline calls, while the hitting-time reduction additionally counts terminal output as position N+2.
oracle_realizations.information_bottleneck: Robust local flatness limits tail disclosure to at most one new frame direction on good prefixes. Conditional rotation and radial control handle adaptive unbounded queries. Public c is only position-1 information.
oracle_realizations.information_to_error: N+2<=T gives joint probability>=3/4 that all base-position gradients exceed delta. Any epsilon-stationary primal output would give base gradient<=delta at the appended terminal position. Average success<=1/4 yields a fixed instance per algorithm with failure>=3/4.
oracle_realizations.query_and_feedback: At arbitrary (x,y), exact f, full joint gradient and full joint Hessian. With w=y-bx-c: f=F(y)-mu||w||^2; gx=2mu b w; gy=grad F(y)-2mu w; Hxx=-2mu b^2 I; Hxy=Hyx^T=2mu b I; Hyy=H_F(y)-2mu I. One baseline all-derivative response at y computes all entries after preprocessing.
oracle_realizations.sampling_and_reuse: One fixed function reused; no resampling, stochastic observations or finite-sum structure.

map: PDF15–17: Definition4, equation10 and Lemmas1–3 define the smooth robust zero-chain. When coordinates j>=i have magnitude<1/2, a neighborhood depends only on coordinates through i. All derivatives/local-germ feedback ignores the remaining tail. If any coordinate has magnitude<1, Lemma2 gives gradient norm>1. Gap<=12T and gradient<=23sqrt(T); B.1–B.2 PDF30–34 provide scalar recurrences and nearest-neighbor tensor estimates.

B.3 PDF34–36, Lemma4a: P_t projects onto span{x1,u1,...,xt,ut}, alpha=1/(5R sqrt(T)), G_t={max_{j>=t}|<u_j,P_(t-1)^perp x_t>|<=alpha||P_(t-1)^perp x_t||}. Gram–Schmidt bounds ||P_(t-1)u_j||^2<=2alpha^2(t-1) on G_<t, giving |<u_j,x_s>|<1/2 on good prefixes. Zero normalization directions can be omitted.

B.3 PDF37–40, Lemmas4b–4c: good-prefix queries depend measurably on seed and exposed columns. Rotations fixing the earlier query/column span preserve the recursively generated transcript and good-prefix event. Conditional projected hidden directions remain uniform on the complement, dimension>=d-2(t-1). Spherical concentration and union bounds give P(G_t^c|G_<t)<=2T exp[-alpha^2(d-2T)/2] and total bad probability<=2T^2 exp[-alpha^2(d-2T)/2]<=eta. Conditional invariance is imported with its source proof, not inferred from unconditional Haar symmetry. The 4b proof prints columns through s-1 while Section5.1 uses through s; only the sufficient through-s exposure convention is used here.

Lemma5 PDF21–23 maps unbounded x_t to y_t=P_R(x_t), ||y_t||<=R. All h derivatives are computable from rotated-chain derivatives there and public radial/quadratic terms. For ||x||<=R/2 a hidden-coordinate gradient is at least 2/sqrt(5)-1/20-1/(2sqrt(5))>1/2. For ||x||>=R/2, ||grad h||>=R/10-(2/sqrt(5))R/10>sqrt(T)>=1. Thus all T informed query gradients exceed 1/2 with probability>=1-eta.

Lemma6 PDF23 and B.4 PDF40–43 give uniform smoothness and gap. B.4 uses partition chain rule, R^(1-k) radial derivative estimates and Bell-number counting. Intermediate all-order formulas are not adopted; the complete local p=1,2 check below suffices. proofs.full_local_argument: From P036 Lemma3/B.2 choose positive uniform K1>=||H_bar_f|| and K2>=||D^3 bar_f||; ||grad bar_f||<=23sqrt(T). Put g=(1+||z||^2/R^2)^(-1/2). DP_R=gI-g^3 zz^T/R^2 has norm<=1. For unit a,b, D2P_R[a,b]=-g^3[(z.a)b+(z.b)a+(a.b)z]/R^2+3g^5(z.a)(z.b)z/R^4. With q=||z||/R, qg<=1 and g<=1 give ||D2P_R||<=6/R. Differentiating gives three zero-z terms with total coefficient 3, six two-z terms with total coefficient 18, and a four-z term with coefficient 15; the same inequalities bound their sum by 36/R^2. The composition chain rule gives ||H_h||<=K1+138/230+1/5<K1+1 and ||D3h||<=K2+18K1/R+828sqrt(T)/R^2<=K2+K1+1, because R=230sqrt(T), T>=1. Set a1=K1+1,a2=K2+K1+1. Line integration gives global Hessian Lipschitzness. All functions are C-infinity. This establishes both required budgets without adopting B.4's displayed alpha^(l) identity; at l=1 the local calculation uses the directly differentiated sign for alpha(r)=sqrt(1+2r). No all-order reproof is claimed.

proofs.full_local_argument: Scaling gives F_U(0)-inf F_U<=12AT=24delta s T<=Delta, ||H_F||<=A a1/s^2=2delta a1/s<=ell, Lip(H_F)<=A a2/s^3=2delta a2/s^2<=rho. F_U is bounded below. A base query sequence z_t rescales to an h-informed sequence z_t/s since derivatives scale by A/s^k; no U information is added. Lemma5 implies, jointly over U and the independent seed, probability>=1-eta that ||grad F_U(z_t)||=(A/s)||grad h_U(z_t/s)||>delta for every t<=T. The distribution and all scales are fixed before algorithm coins. Query position1 is 0, computing g0 and public c; this U-dependent information is part of the permitted transcript, not uncharged advice. Simulate N bundles with base queries at each y, then append uhat=b*xhat+c as position N+2. Early stopping can be padded to N before this terminal position. All maps remain measurable and N+2<=T lets Lemma5 cover them. The linked complete quadratic transfer gives ||grad Phi_U(xhat)||<=epsilon => ||grad F_U(uhat)||<=delta. Thus success averaged over U is<=eta=1/4. For each algorithm some fixed U has success<=1/4 over its seed, hence failure>=3/4, independently of the realized seed. This is not one publicly known function hard for every algorithm. If T>=3 and N<=T-2, uniform per-instance success>=2/3 is impossible. Write B=Delta/(24delta s)=(Delta/24)min{ell/(2a1delta^2),sqrt(rho/(2a2))*delta^(-3/2)}. For sufficiently large B, floor and the two positions are absorbed, giving T=Theta(Delta min{ell delta^-2,sqrt(rho)delta^-3/2}). For kappa>=6, b^2=Theta(kappa), mu b^2=Theta(L); the lifted lower rate is Omega(Delta min{L epsilon^-2,sqrt(rho)kappa^(3/4)epsilon^-3/2}). For 1<=kappa<6 instead use ell=L,delta=epsilon and f_U(x,y)=F_U(x)-mu||y||^2/2. Then Phi=F_U, y*(0)=0, gap<=Delta, joint Hessian is block diagonal with norm<=L, and its Lipschitz constant<=rho. One base response at x simulates a complete bundle; no shift preprocessing is required, so terminal output is position N+1 and N+1<=T suffices. Bounded kappa factors give the same displayed baseline order.
